To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dual scattering channel schemes extend Johns' TLM algorithm in two directions: (a) transmission line links are abstracted to scattering channels and (b) non-trivial cell interfaces are admitted during the connection cycles.

the dual scattering channel method is an abstract, general and efficient time-domain numerical method for the simulation of Maxwell and diffusion type problems, and that it is particularly suitable for the simulation of electromagnetic and thermal problems in complex geometries, such as the human body, at frequencies from 1 Hz to 10 GHz.

(i) the Johns' algorithm is extended to abstract scattering channels; (ii) the Johns' connection cycle is generalized by allowing for arbitrary scattering at cell interfaces; (iii) a DSC scheme is presented that allows to couple heat and electromagnetic field propagation in a single non-orthogonal grid; (iv) the DSC scheme is extended to a non-linear, lossy Maxwell field.
